conventions.statement: Each table fills one grid unit-square cell and offers one possible chair per side accessible from the exterior.
Each shared full-edge join makes both opposing chair sides unusable.
An unshared side facing a fully enclosed vacant courtyard cannot hold a chair approached from outside.
Removing a noncorner outer border table can connect the courtyard to the exterior and make its formerly inaccessible sides available.

exit_task.prompt: Independently model a 3x3 ring of square tables with the middle cell empty and sealed. Determine n, e, inaccessible inward-facing sides c and accessible chair sites. Explain why unshared sides alone overcounts.

answer.summary: n=8, e=8, c=4 and A=12 accessible exterior sides.
reasoning: Eight occupied cells form a cycle with eight shared full-side contacts.
Thirty-two candidate sides minus sixteen sides at shared contacts gives sixteen unshared sides.
Four of those unshared sides border the sealed central cell and are not externally accessible.
Therefore A=32−16−4=12; direct outer perimeter also has 12 unit edges.
answer.check: The outside of a 3×3 square has perimeter12.

boundary_test.prompt: On a closed 3x3 table ring n=8,e=8,c=4. Remove the top-middle table, opening its center: verify new n=7,e=6,c=0 and find the outside-accessible chair sites.
boundary_test.answer: Closed A=4×8−2×8−4=12; opened A=4×7−2×6=16, because the center is now exterior-connected.

questions.stem: Two non-coprime repeating phases require x≡2 (mod6) and x≡5 (mod9). Check the compatibility condition, reduce the congruence and verify the full solution class.
conditions: Both schedules must be satisfied simultaneously.

reasoning: Write x=2+6t, then 6t≡3 modulo9, reducing to 2t≡1 modulo3.
t≡2 modulo3; x=14+18k, and x=14 checks both phases.

questions.failure_signal: Blindly multiplying non-coprime periods misses gcd feasibility and correct lcm repetition.

family_exposure.closure: Concept anchor cannot substitute for three-period Core2A protected application.

grade9v3:cognitive_demand.basis: Execute a conditional known modular procedure on non-standard triple with compatibility exceptions and bounded output; W is method choice and correct application.

grade9v3:analysis.stable_crux_move: At each combination test gcd divisibility, reduce correctly and stop if a changed phase is incompatible.
grade9v3:analysis.common_wrong_route: Use coprime CRT or product periods blindly, then search an impossible system.

questions.stem: A system admits an integer service slot x only when ALL three repeating phases hold: x≡5 (mod12), x≡11 (mod18), and x≡9 (mod20). The service window is the inclusive interval 200≤x≤600. Apply a VALID compatibility-aware method to find every eligible integer slot. Explicitly check the gcd condition each time you combine constraints, reduce the congruences correctly, give the final repeating class and verify every listed slot. Do not assume pairwise-coprime CRT applies.
conditions: x is an integer with 200≤x≤600 inclusive.
All three given congruences must hold simultaneously.
Periods 12,18,20 are positive but not pairwise coprime.

answer.summary: All eligible integer slots are 209,389,569; the combined class is x≡29 modulo180.
reasoning: First screen gcd(12,18)=6 dividing 11−5=6. The pair is compatible. Write x=5+12t, so 12t≡6 modulo18; divide all terms by6 to get 2t≡1 modulo3 and t≡2 modulo3.
Therefore x=5+12(2+3k)=29+36k, the first two conditions combined as x≡29 modulo36.

Second screen gcd(36,20)=4 dividing the third-phase difference 9−29=−20. The third condition is compatible. Substitute 29+36k≡9 modulo20, so 16k≡0 modulo20; divide all terms by4 to get 4k≡0 modulo5, implying k≡0 modulo5.
Thus x=29+180j, repeating with lcm(36,20)=180. In 200≤x≤600 the admissible j are 1,2,3, producing 209,389,569; j=0 gives29 below and j=4 gives749 above.
Verify each of 209,389,569 leaves residues5 modulo12,11 modulo18 and9 modulo20.

reasoning_route.action: Represent the three phases and the inclusive interval; reject blind coprime CRT.
reasoning_route.why_valid: The periods share factors and compatibility must precede inverse-based reduction.

reasoning_route.action: Check gcd(12,18)=6 divides 11−5; then combine to x≡29 modulo36.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Substitution x=5+12t yields 2t≡1 mod3; gcd screen establishes feasibility.

reasoning_route.action: Screen gcd(36,20)=4 and reduce the third condition to k≡0 modulo5, or stop if incompatible.
reasoning_route.why_valid: 9−29=−20 is divisible by4, so compatibility permits the reduction.

reasoning_route.action: Intersect x=29+180j with inclusive [200,600], then check each original phase.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Inequalities yield integer j=1,2,3 and substitution confirms all requirements.

answer.check: 209%12=5, %18=11, %20=9; 389 and569 repeat with period180. 29 is below interval,749 above.

scaffolds.text: Before solving, write all three phases as simultaneous congruences, and decide whether pairwise-coprime CRT can be used without modification.
Combine just the first two conditions using gcd(12,18). Is the residue difference compatible? Use a substitution x=5+12t, then keep the lcm as the new period.
Only AFTER your own attempt: audit whether your first combined residue agrees with the third residue modulo the new gcd; reduce the resulting linear congruence and intersect the class with [200,600].

questions.failure_signal: Blind product periods, omitted gcd screen on the third phase, incorrect modular division, or missing one interval endpoint indicates a method-selection error.

family_exposure.closure: Independent mastery requires screening both non-coprime combinations, producing the correct class and all bounded slots without post-attempt help.

independent_check.statement: Enumerate all x in inclusive [200,600] by direct residues, compare with 29+180k, and independently check all solutions of pair 5 mod12,11 mod18 over a full lcm period.

difficulty.basis: Conditional method selection across three non-coprime periods and interval, with a later changed phase that invalidates applicability.

component_evidence.concept_model_selection: Choose compatibility-first generalized CRT, not the coprime formula.
component_evidence.representation_translation: Translate repeating constraints and interval to congruence class.
component_evidence.reasoning_chain_length: Reduce first pair, test third, reduce again, enumerate bounded arithmetic progression.
component_evidence.algebra_computational_load: Small modular arithmetic and three interval outputs.
component_evidence.trap_exception_sensitivity: Third condition can become incompatible after a single phase change.

grade9v3:cognitive_demand.basis: Adapt a conditional algorithm to a changed infeasible input then recompute after a valid repair.

grade9v3:analysis.stable_crux_move: Check gcd compatibility before every solve; stop when 4∤−19.
grade9v3:analysis.common_wrong_route: Continue with previous answer class or invent an impossible slot.

questions.stem: A single schedule is changed. Keep x≡5 (mod12), x≡11 (mod18), and the SAME inclusive interval 200≤x≤600, but replace the third phase with x≡10 (mod20). Apply your compatibility-first procedure to decide whether ANY slot exists; do not blindly search the interval if the gcd screen fails. An engineer then proposes replacing 10 by 13 modulo20. Test that repair and find ALL slots in [200,600] for the repaired system. State the new combined class.
conditions: The first two congruences are unchanged.
Changed third residue10 modulo20 must be evaluated separately.
A proposed repair replaces residue10 with13 modulo20, not the old residue9.

answer.summary: Changed residue10 is impossible; corrected residue13 gives x≡173 modulo180 and exactly slots353,533 in [200,600].
reasoning: The unchanged first pair remains x≡29 modulo36.
With third residue10 modulo20, gcd(36,20)=4 would need to divide 10−29=−19; it does not. Therefore no x can satisfy all constraints, regardless of how large the interval is.
If the third phase is corrected to13 modulo20, difference13−29=−16 is divisible by4, so the combined system is compatible.
Set x=29+36k. Require 29+36k≡13 mod20, hence 16k≡4 modulo20, reducing to 4k≡1 modulo5. Since 4 is its own inverse modulo5, k≡4 modulo5.
Thus x=29+36(4+5j)=173+180j. Within [200,600], j=1,2 yields x=353,533. Check both candidates against phases5 modulo12,11 modulo18 and13 modulo20.

reasoning_route.action: Keep unchanged first-pair residue29 modulo36 and the interval.
Test changed residue10 for gcd compatibility and STOP immediately when it fails.
reasoning_route.why_valid: 4 does not divide10−29=−19; the congruences are globally inconsistent.
reasoning_route.output: No integer solution, independent of window.

reasoning_route.action: Retest residue13, reduce 16k≡4 mod20 and recompute combined class.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Difference13−29=−16 passes divisibility by4, and k≡4 mod5.

reasoning_route.action: Intersect repaired class with window and verify direct residue checks.

answer.check: For x=353 and533, residues (mod12,18,20) are (5,11,13); no x can satisfy old first-pair residue29 mod36 with third residue10 mod20.

rubric.criterion: Reject changed residue10 with a gcd divisibility obstruction.
rubric.evidence_of: No futile numerical search or invented slot.

rubric.criterion: Screen repaired residue13 then re-solve correctly.
Find exactly the repaired interval solutions and check all phases.

hints.text: Start from the first-pair combined class and compare its residue to 10 modulo gcd(36,20) BEFORE enumerating. The correction to13 requires a new modular reduction.

questions.failure_signal: Finding a numeric slot for incompatible residue10 or recycling 209,389,569 after correction13 is failure to re-run the conditional algorithm.

family_exposure.closure: Changed-input transfer is independent only if the incompatibility is detected without search and the repaired branch is genuinely recomputed.

independent_check.statement: Exhaust all integer x over one period180 and [200,600]; changed third residue10 has zero solutions; corrected residue13 yields class173 modulo180 and slots353,533.

difficulty.basis: Applying the conditional algorithm to a changed infeasible phase, then recomputing a nontrivial corrected phase under the same interval.

component_evidence.concept_model_selection: Stop at gcd incompatibility without searching, then restart for a compatible correction.
component_evidence.representation_translation: Carry first-pair class to two alternative third phases.
component_evidence.reasoning_chain_length: Obstruction test, repaired congruence reduction, new interval intersection.
component_evidence.algebra_computational_load: Small residues modulo4,5 and bounded class.
component_evidence.trap_exception_sensitivity: Changing 9 to10 destroys all solutions, while correction13 creates a different set.

transfer.statement: Changed phase causes a genuine impossible branch; proposed correction makes a different feasible class.
transfer.invariant: The first pair still gives x≡29 mod36, and gcd(36,20)=4 must divide third difference.

novelty.why_new: The learner must refuse a previously valid procedure at residue10 then restart it for corrected residue13; neither branch is the former x≡29 mod180.
